question: Should recording publication evidence for an already-published version keep requiring the exact release runtime pin (Node v24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, zlib 1.3.2.1-motley-3246f1b), or should the pin be narrowed to the steps whose byte result depends on the toolchain, with evidence recording requiring only a minimum npm version?
options: Keep the exact pin on evidence recording, as before (status quo)

Narrow the pin: keep it exact for every step whose byte result depends on the toolchain, and require only npm major version 11 or newer, checked at the start of every evidence recording run, for evidence recording
Drop every runtime requirement from evidence recording, including the npm floor
recommendation: Option 2, the narrowing that the read-only analysis in foundry issue #1659 supported: the recording path never packs, qualifies or writes a package tarball, so the exact tuple protects nothing there. It downloads the published tarball, compares hashes and integrity, reads the archived qualification transcript, and checks git ancestry. Two of its steps do depend on the npm in use, so it needs a recent npm: npm audit signatures --include-attestations (the v3 replay and the automatic workflow's provenance pre-check) and, for a schema-3 qualification, npm pack --dry-run. Correction: the first version of this record named only the audit as the toolchain-sensitive step. Review found that incomplete, and that the hand-run direct join had no check at all; the floor now covers all of them.
decision: On 2026-09-29 the owner delegated this call in chat with the words "make the right pin decision for me, then execute", after the read-only analysis in foundry issue #1659. The master session made the call under that delegation on 2026-09-29, using that analysis: option 2. Narrowed scope: recording publication evidence for an already-published version (createLaterPublicationRecord in scripts/record-later-publication.mjs, reached by the direct join, the v3 replay and the command line) no longer calls assertReleaseRuntime. Instead, at the start of createLaterPublicationRecord, right after the credential-free check and before any input is read, the recorder resolves npm once to an absolute path from PATH, refusing to resolve it through a relative or empty PATH entry, and reads that npm's version. It refuses, with a clear message, when the npm major version is below 11, when the version cannot be read, or when the output is not exactly one semantic version (for example 11.0.0garbage or multi-line output). The same absolute npm runs npm audit signatures --include-attestations, and verifiedAnonymousAudit re-reads its version immediately before running it, which also covers the automatic workflow's provenance pre-check. The floor therefore covers the direct join, the v3 replay, and the workflow. For a schema-3 qualification the qualification join also runs npm pack --dry-run (currentQualificationJoins in scripts/lib/candidate-qualification.mjs); the recorder does not run that command itself, so it is covered by the same floor through the first npm on the process's own PATH, not through the resolved path. Unchanged: the exact pin in scripts/lib/release-runtime.mjs remains required, with no change to its values, for qualification (run-candidate-qualification.mjs, candidate-runner.mjs), packing and artifact reproducibility (artifact-reproducibility.mjs), publishing (publish-qualified-directory.mjs, publish-qualified-set.mjs) and retention. The setup-node pin and the assert step in .github/workflows/record-publication-evidence.yml are unchanged, so automated evidence records are still produced on the exact tuple; only a comment there was updated. This decision does not authorize relaxing the pin for any step whose byte result depends on the toolchain.
notes: CHAT CHANNEL, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE: this record cites an owner chat message and cannot be checked against anything in this repository. THE DECISION WAS DELEGATED, NOT TYPED AS A SPECIFIC OPTION BY THE OWNER: the owner wrote only the delegation quoted in `decision`; the choice of option 2 and its exact scope were made by the master session under that delegation, so `decidedBy: owner` records the delegated authority, not an owner-selected option. The `recommendation` restates the master session's summary of the #1659 analysis, corrected after review, and was not independently re-read when this record was written; `reviews` is empty because no reviewer identities were captured for that analysis. JUDGMENT CALLS: (1) `relaxesGateOrPolicy` is true. The change replaces an exact-match refusal on the recording path with a weaker minimum-version check, which loosens an existing check. The argument that the pin never protected anything on this path is plausible but is the kind of self-serving characterization the contract warns about, so the record declares the loosening and lets the sunset bound it. (2) `sunset` and `expiry` are both 2027-03-29, about six months after the decision. The contract forces a non-null sunset and a non-null expiry for a relaxation, so those values are contract-valid rather than derived from any owner-stated duration; the date is the master session's choice of a review interval for the pin's scope. Only a later record whose `supersedes` names this one clears the sunset flag once the date passes; reverting the code does not. Renewing or reversing the narrowing is therefore a new superseding record. scripts/check-decision-records.mjs is not run by CI (no workflow or package script runs it; it is run by hand), so nothing fails automatically after the sunset: the flag appears only when someone runs that script, and the code stays narrowed until then. scripts/land-stack.mjs only stops counting an expired or sunset record as tier-2 authority, which has no effect here because this record authorizes nothing (see 3). Someone must remember to supersede or renew this record before 2027-03-29. (3) `links.pullRequests` and `links.paths` are empty on purpose. scripts/land-stack.mjs reads decision records from a pull request's base commit, so a record added by the same pull request cannot authorize that pull request, and a pull-request link would also require a pinned patch-id that cannot include the record itself. A path link would pre-authorize future changes to those paths until the expiry. The pull request that adds this record touches tier-2 paths (scripts/lib/release-runtime.mjs, scripts/lib/publication-evidence-run.mjs, scripts/lib/publication-evidence-run.test.mjs, and this file under governance/decisions/**), so it needs the owner's own merge, or the owner's explicit approval in chat of the exact head being merged. The delegation above was given before this diff existed and does not, on its own, cover merging it; the merge-train gate is report-only today and would not block a merge mechanically, so this rests on the owner. `links.issues` names #1659.
